checks.what: wu_-750 (-750..-585): {place: Suzhou, km: 60} replaced by {lon 120.62, lat 31.30, km 60}. Gazetteer: the old place spec resolves to Suzhou, Anhui (116.98E 33.64N, 60 cells on the Huai); the new union Wuxi 60 km + Suzhou (Jiangsu) point resolves to 82 cells (about 20,700 km2, 119.69-121.23E, 30.81-32.00N), the Wuxi-Suzhou core only, against 116 cells in two discs before. Page: infobox 'Capital: Wu (modern-day Wuxi and Suzhou, Jiangsu province)'; 'Its first capital was at Meili (in modern Wuxi)', 'then Helu's City (... near Wuxi)', 'and later moved to Gusu (probably in modern Suzhou)'. The keyframe starts at -750, so the corrected disc also applies -750..-701 (m0800-m0701), which is the same correct fix; wu_-1100 keeps the Anhui homonym (dossier request already filed).

kingdom-of-kush_-700 (-700..-676) cut from Cliopatria's -700 Kush shape (1,956 cells, Nubia plus all Egypt) to the -675 shape (1,195 cells, Nubia to 23.74N; its non-Egyptian part 986 cells against 983 for the -700 shape minus Egypt, so no Nubian land lost). Egypt stays drawn by twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt_-712 (Nile Valley, -712..-672), which removes the double drawing (dynasty ribbon inside a Kush desert donut). Page: the dynasty is 'a line of pharaohs who originated in the Kingdom of Kush'; 'Shebitku conquered the entire Nile Valley, including Upper and Lower Egypt, around 712 BC'. The page treats Kush and Egypt as one Kushite realm ('Kushite power stretched from the Mediterranean Sea to the present Ethiopian boundary'); the project splits it into two dossiers, and together they still cover Nubia plus the Nile Valley. The Egyptian deserts become unowned, which the dynasty dossier's Nile Valley reading implies. The -701/-700 seam (Kush holds the deserts at the start anchor via m0800-m0701's ledger gain of the region 'Upper Egypt', 2,359 cells with New Valley and Red Sea) is m0800-m0701's to trim.

kingdom-of-kush_-675 (-675..-651): union of the -675 Kush shape with the region 'Upper Egypt' (2,359 cells, whole governorates incl. New Valley and Red Sea desert) replaced by the -675 Kush shape alone (Nubia, 1,195 cells). Upper Egypt stays with the dynasty's own keyframes -671, -667 and -663 (Upper and Middle Egypt, to -656). Page: 'However, Taharqa was defeated in Egypt in 671 BC when Esarhaddon conquered Northern Egypt, captured Memphis, imposed tribute, and then withdrew'; Tantamani row: 'Lost control of Upper Egypt in 656 BC when Psamtik I captured Thebes in that year' (both quotes verified verbatim). Not made worse by the patch but still open: Kush's own ledger events 6 and 8 (-669 and -664 gains of Lower Egypt) keep giving Kush the Delta in the years the dynasty's keyframes -669 and -664 claim it (see problems).

neo-assyrian-empire_-675 (-675..-656): minus {country: Egypt} in place of minus {region: Upper Egypt}; 2,840 cells against 3,341 (the 501 removed cells are Sinai, the Delta, the Matruh coast and Middle Egypt). Consistent with the neighbouring keyframes: Cliopatria's -700 Assyria shape has 0 cells in Egypt, and the dossier's own -655 keyframe already uses the same 'minus Egypt' spec; the 671 ledger gain (Nile Valley minus Upper Egypt) still brings Memphis and the Delta in. Page: 'His first attack in 677 ... led him as far as the Brook of Egypt' (a campaign, not a holding), 'Taharqa and his army defeated the Assyrians outright in 674', 'Esarhaddon raided Egypt in 673', 'In 671, Esarhaddon took and sacked Memphis'; the page names no Assyrian holding in Egypt or Sinai before 671 (no mention of Sinai, Arish or Arza).

lydia_-650 given years -650..-621 (Cliopatria's -650..-631); shape unchanged (98,905 km2, Troad, Hellespont coast, Caria), as the dossier's own correction text asks. Page: Cimmerians 'warred with Lydia, which eventually expelled them by around 620 BC, and then expanded to incorporate much of Phrygia, which became the Lydian empire's eastern frontier' (the expansion stated as after the expulsion). Lydia's ledger gains of Phrygia and of Mysia/Bithynia/Paphlagonia are dated -620, matching.

lydia_-630 given years -620..-616 (Cliopatria's -630..-616); shape unchanged (255,588 km2 to the Halys). Same Phrygia page sentence: expulsion 'by around 620 BC', 'and then expanded to incorporate much of Phrygia'; removes a 556-cell snap ten years before the dated expansion. lydia_-615 still begins at -615, so no gap.
